correctness.rationale: The stationary balance S=1/R, I=aJ, C=JB(v), V=fb yields J=K/(a+B(v)) and the exact budget equation. Differentiating G(v) gives 1/R+K(B²+aE[Te^{-vT}])/(a+B)²>0, hence a unique positive root and consistent compartments for every allowed law. Two Hermite quadratics yield sharp all-hazard Laplace bounds from identical first two moments; strictness and the decreasing B(v) propagate them through endogenous hazard roots to sharp incidence/prevalence bounds with unique two-point equality laws. A standalone standard-library checker passed 1728 finite corroborative assertions. Assumptions and boundary restrictions are explicit.

originality.rationale: The exact model and its fixed-v stationary transform are prior art (Yang–Saldaña–Scoglio, arXiv:2303.15326); general two-moment Hermite inequalities are also classical. The final claim is instead the sharp incidence envelope for every natural-immunity law with fixed support, mean and variance when the **realized administered-dose flux** rather than hazard is held fixed, including existence/uniqueness of the endogenous calibrated stationary hazard. Searches of relevant public records and comparison with accessible full primary SIRVS and heterogeneous-immunity texts did not identify a direct or dominating theorem. Priority remains provisional because some related primary full texts were inaccessible.
residual_risks: The full text of arXiv:2306.13633 and Carr immunity-moment work was not materially inspected; cannot exclude implicit specialized general results from them.
Classical bounded two-moment extremal-distribution theory may make the transform step familiar; novelty depends on the full realized-dose budget epidemiological implication, not that algebraic tool.
Complete global publication priority and independent scientific verification have not been established.

value.rationale: Dose supplies are naturally specified by actual administered throughput rather than individual eligible-person hazard; endemic eligibility depends on the unknown natural-immunity law, making fixed-hazard optimizations not directly policy-comparable. The theorem provides sharp computable worst/best stationary infection-incidence and prevalence limits knowing only natural-duration support, mean and variance, with explicit distinct extremal duration laws and a single monotone scalar equation per endpoint. It identifies a meaningful data-limitation gap without claiming arbitrary population or dynamic generality.
